what: When an AI agent's pull request in the public AIDev dataset adds a PyPI or npm dependency its task did not name (a new-dependency extra under the frozen rules v6), how much does that one line bring along on a fresh install? Unit: one line, the first such extra of a pull request (so no pull request counts twice). Sample: pull requests in the order of random.Random(20261019) over all AIDev pull request ids, scanned until 300 lines are found.
measure: The CI job's own lookup, today (itemator/registry.py look_up_one, itemator/weight.py): the pinned version, else the registry's latest; deps.dev's resolved graph; the download size of each package from its registry (PyPI: the wheel pip would most likely pick on Linux x86_64 with CPython 3.12, else the source archive; npm: the tarball). Bytes and package counts are measured; nothing is estimated.
outputs: median and 90th percentile of packages per line (the line's own package included) and of download bytes
lines bringing 10 or more packages, lines with 10 MB or more
the same for lines in merged pull requests, and their total bytes
limits: Today's graph and today's versions, not the ones the pull request saw; deps.dev's resolver, not a lockfile; download bytes, not installed bytes or energy; one line per pull request; PyPI and npm only (deps.dev gives no Go or NuGet graph and its Cargo graph includes dev-only dependencies). Nothing here says a dependency was wrong to add: it says what keeping it costs each fresh install.
stop_rules: one run; no re-run for a result we dislike; a platform failure before any line is weighed may be re-run once, logged
no Duo credits: no flow runs
